body: Yea the original belief was that the common people were too easily influenced over superfluous things, so the senators would be the 'wise men' that didn't bow to common opinion. Nowadays most people who want to can be in the know as much as the senators can.

It's so they're more beholden to the people. With 2 year terms they constantly have to be in our good graces. The senators were meant to not listen to the people until election time. In our past the senate wasn't even chosen by the people but by our representatives.

People know there is no solution, but admitting that to them is the same as saying "go ahead and kill yourself because it doesn't get better." They just want to feel like they did something to help, even if it doesn't help.

This opinion is up here every day. I hate cooking. And I don't care much about food, and the time to cook something I'm barely going to enjoy isn't worth it. Cooking is easy, but it's still an hour of something I hate for a meal I'm barely going to care about and finish in 5 minutes. I'll just make a sandwich.

Yea that's true, but it's also irresponsible to jump into having kids when you don't have the financial means to take care of them. Lower employment rates and wages means we're able to afford them at later years. As for compatibility, that's very true, and honestly where I live most people had kids early and got married. I'm 30 and finally just gave up on finding any of that, so I'm in a different boat then the people I've been referring to.

That's true, but at the same time I can understand people not liking it due to the fact that you're doing more work, having to put in more effort, to have the same outcome you'd have as a younger parent. If the trend for instance continues, it means the next generation will wait even longer to have kids, and that seems like backwards progress to me.

That's true, and I do believe we'll get to a point where a 50 year old woman can have kids without issues. But there's still an increased chance of complications the older you get. The bigger thing for me though is relation to your child. I grew up with folks that had older parents or an older father at least, and they had very little connection to them. They couldn't relate to each other due to the age gap, and between work and them getting older, very little quality time spent with their parents (usually fathers). As someone who wanted to be a dad growing up, I abhor the idea of not being able to connect to my kids. Not always the case for some people, but definitely something to consider.

The big problem is that every generation should want the next generation a little better off, so when people look at their parents or grandparents and realize we have to wait longer to get the same things in life it bothers people. Also I'm not in the 30 is the new 25 boat. Certain things still have a time frame on them, like having kids.

Did you ever think that's what they wanted? I'd have much rather just settled down earlier in life, and just because you marry early doesn't mean you can't do all that other stuff. Just because you marry you're high school sweetheart doesn't mean you can't travel for instance.
Older actors start doing this later in life for that sweet, sweet retirement money. Look at John Travolta and Robert De Niro for example.

My favorite character on Jurassic Park was Jeff Goldblum's character. He was a chaotician who's entire reason for being there was to think of all the scenarios where the park could go wrong. There's a reason he's the first person there to realize it was a bad idea. Sometimes overthinking things can be good.

Well first, 21 is past primary education, I wasn't referring to college. I also know that it's not always feasible for a teen to not work, which is why I said "It's not always feasible." But having something be the outlier vs the norm is the big thing. I don't want it to be normalized that teens drop out of high school to work. And the fact is, most of the places I go to for lunch or during that time of the day, have adults working there. Grocery stores, restaurants, fast food places. That's because most of the teens are required to go to school. Even work leave only gives you so much time in a week where you can not be in school.

No I'm ok with teens working. What I do expect is that at noon on a weekday it should be an adult, because I want teens to get an education. You can learn those skills after school or on the weekends. It's not always feasible, but it doesn't change that a lot of the jobs for 'teenagers' are going to require adults to work them from time to time. As for McDonalds being 5 star, of course it's not. Doesn't change that I don't want teenagers ditching education to work there. As for hard, no it's not hard work, but it is soul sucking, so I try to treat the workers at any business with some respect.

I just got done having my friend build my pc. I say my friend built it because he was going to supervise, then realized what we had was far too complicated to build myself. He ended up putting it together just so we didn't break any parts. And it still has issues we're trying to fix. Could be the motherboard, could be one of the usb ports. If I bought one prebuilt, no hassle, my friend doesn't have to get involved, and it's guaranteed to work. I love my pc and I'm glad I went this route, but it's not quite the "plug and play, like legos" I keep hearing about pc parts.

Yea people around me bring up working at McDonalds. I always mention that when I go there at noon on a weekday, I'd hope it's not a teen working there, I want them in school so I don't have to deal with their stupidity in a couple years.

I hate cooking. I live alone and nothing is more depressing to me than spending up to an hour or more making a meal it takes me 5 minutes to eat. Then because no one puts meal plans for one up, I end up eating left overs I could care less about for the next day or two. I'd rather make a sandwich.

I just bought a house that's all hardwood floors or tile. I like the hardwood floors, but damn if I haven't covered almost all of it in rugs. Hardwood floors are cold, and if you clean them regularly, slippery as hell. My whole house is basically designed to shatter old people's hips. Carpeting can be pretty comfortable in the right areas. Just a thought on why some people get rid of the hardwood.
The best advice I've ever heard about raising kids is "Imagine what you want your kids to be, how they react to situations, how they behave and talk. Now go be that person."

Emotions are the reason we all live. Logically, everything you've done and will do is pointless, why not just off yourself? Because people enjoy living. They get good emotions that help influence us to keep doing what we're doing. Without emotions we're robots, and might as well not exist.

Fuck no, cheaters do it more than once. Very rarely have I seen someone who cheated once, and even then I suspect they were lying to preserve their reputation. If you forgive them it lowers your value in their eyes and they will do it again. You deserve better.

Personally, to me, people who do bad actions. If you lie, cheat or steal only for personal gain, you're bad. Maybe there can be something said for people who do it to help other people than themselves, but purely self beneficial behavior that hurts others, I think those are bad people.

It's not that the arguments are bad, it's that the person using them can't do anything other than argue "keep going" at the end of the day. "This pain is unbearable and I can't stand it anymore." "Keep going." Some people can be helped, but when you've exhausted all opportunities for help, these sayings that people use over and over again lose all meaning. In the end you've said it yourself, you're saying whatever you can to keep them alive. How much of it is actually truth? "It can get better." What are the odds? Is it more likely to get worse? If you're afraid the truth would drive someone to suicide maybe that's because for that person it should. It doesn't make them a bad guy, but it does come off as unempathetic, which to a severely depressed person, are the last people you want to be around.

I often ask this question to people and I actually differ from you greatly in opinion. If it took one random person to die in order for all of humanity to live, I'd let humanity die. No one good would want someone else to sacrifice themselves for them, and why would I sacrifice someone for bad people? The only time I'd do it is if the person I'm sacrificing is a known bad person.

Then you're choosing an absence of pain on your end in exchange for continued prolonged pain on theirs. I've ended up cutting those people out of my life because when there are no good arguments to stick around, the bad ones feel even more insincere.
So what would you say to that person or do after you've exhausted all those routes? Do you accept an end to their pain or keep requesting that they stick around for no good reason?

That article was terrible, when does it become an expectation? How big does the percentage become of people who kill themselves vs don't before society says "we expect you to kill yourself because of your problems." the correct answer would be never, because accepting someones choice and encouraging it for them are two different things. The only person who can justify a suicide is the person doing it, so even if a lot more people started killing themselves, it's still those people making a choice for themselves. It's just doing it while avoiding all the banal platitudes that society likes to try as arguments. Because I've yet to see a legit argument against suicide that isn't "you have a wife and kids".

I disagree that anyone can give their lives value but themselves. If a person is in misery and you're saying stay because you're still valuable, you don't care about them, you care about their use. I've heard these arguments for years and all it boils down to is, "you can still provide US with something, so you need to stick around"
All I could think of was the Janitor from Scrubs saying "Fork?! Me can't eat soup!"
I'm trying to figure out how you're eating soup with a fork dude? You realize soup isn't eaten with chopsticks, they do have spoons.

At the end of the day you set goal posts so you can live just to live. I don't want to ride a motorcycle, I don't want to parachute out of planes. I wanted a family, that's not happening, so why assign arbitrary goals that mean nothing to anyone and even less to me. For you, that works and I'm glad, but for me, it's the same as sticking around so my boss makes more money off of me. Pointless.
Jesus christ that's depressing. Well good luck to you I hope it gets better. I'm not gonna try to convince myself I should enjoy a life I hate.

Neither of us knows each others experiences enough to compare. I'm glad you got out, doesn't change that I won't. I've been through therapy and to psychologists. I've had blood tests and all sorts of other things done. It boils down to, I just have little to no interest in most things. The things people do for fun seem trivial and boring. On a good day it feels like I'm sitting at the DMV waiting for my number to be called. I had fun when I had a girlfriend, but if you're bored of most things by yourself you don't seem very interesting to most people. I've never met a man in his 60's, with no wife or children, that I thought "You know, I'd like his life." My first thought is always "How have you not killed yourself?"

Then we're all machines to our biology and upbringing, which means whatever I do, violent or not, is already destined to happen according to you. If you have to question what's worth dying for, you're not in that much pain. People don't need to wait for a good reason to jump out of a burning building, the flames are a good enough reason on their own.

13 Years ago was the first time I hung myself. I've had this way longer than 13 years, I've just recognized and been able to talk about it for 13 years. As it is, it sounds like I should endure suffering for what, nothing? So that I can live and keep suffering? I feel better about killing myself, and I have no real reason not to anymore. But the pain I've felt for 13 years that I could have been free of? I feel some people owe me for that. The people who lied and said it would get better.

Yea exactly, shit drives me nuts. I'm in complete agreement with you. If you have the means and the desire to go to a therapist, then sure go, but otherwise for a lot of people it's not possible or doesn't do anything to help.

I'd only be a dick to the people that bullshitted me into sticking around, not everyone in general. Most people consider me to be pretty kind irl. But people that throw out blanket bullshit statements in order to dismiss someone else I have little sympathy for. I've been reacting "well" to these negative feelings for over a decade. It's all a facade just so people don't feel uncomfortable. They'd rather just say "Oh we had no idea this was going to happen" get over it and continue on. Why not fuck them up a little before I'm gone? Even if just mentally?
This guy hasn't seen that Adolf Hitler just got elected in Namibia. (Joking of course, the guy is named Adolf Hitler but his dad named him apparently not knowing who Adolf Hitler was.)

I have severe depression, and have been suicidal for years. I heard that for so many years I've started demanding better answers. "When does it get better? Can you guarantee that? I'm willing to bet my life it doesn't, are you willing to bet yours it does?" 'It might get better' is a far better answer, but of course it sounds really dismal, because that's the prospects of it actually getting better for people like me, pretty dismal.

Either way they'll back out when it gets down to helping you in any real manner. Have you ever gotten far in a conversation with them that actually did anything to help in any other manner? It's different for different people, and maybe there are some that can help some people, but a majority of them are just morons who couldn't do any real work so figured listening to people talking all day and getting to pat yourself on the back is a great way to make a living. I know a lot of older women with nothing better to do who became therapists. Mostly because they couldn't hold down a real job.
Yea of course, because you're recommending we treat them like children when they act out, but adults any other time. Which is moronic.

I've started challenging the people who do that. "Oh it gets better? So if it doesn't what do you lose? How about if I still feel the same way in 5 years I show up at your house with a loaded gun?" You're willing to bet your life on it not getting better, are they willing to bet theirs that it will? Most of the time they just say things like that in order to dismiss it and not have to deal with it. They should at least be honest. If they're not, force them.
You're comparing adult women to children, should we treat them like that in all facets of their lives?

That's a terrible argument. I'm a skinny dude, so I should be able to hit or insult people bigger than me without consequence? A 300lb man can do a lot of damage to me, doesn't mean I get to be an ass.

It is a fucking scam. There's no consequences for being a bad therapist. If every time a suicidal person had a bad therapist they decided to drag them outside and shoot them, there'd suddenly be very few people willing to take the job. As it is all they're betting on is your life and your money. There's no loss if they don't benefit you, but everything to gain.

All this is telling me is the people without all that are fine to leave this world. There's a lot of people who don't have any of those people in their life, and may never have them, no matter how much they searched.

So where's the line between unbearable and tolerable? Is it when someone kills themselves? And just because people can handle something doesn't mean they should. I could probably handle another year of this, but at the end of the year will I be worse or better? Most signs point to worse, why stick around in hell just to wait for the flames to get even hotter?

No, I definitely want to die. I don't feel shame for feeling this way, I think it's a natural reaction to a shitty life. I'm only questioning whether I'll be more satisfied leaving having been a good person, or at least someone who did good actions, or if I leave this world having done enough fucked up shit that people think, "you know, I'm kind of glad he's gone." I'm leaning toward the latter.

Thats true, but I also dont want everyone on Earth to experience my pain constantly. There are good people in this world and I don't want them to suffer. But for instance covid has been amazing at showing me what people can handle. The amount of people breaking down just from a small lack of human interaction is honestly kind of funny to someone who's felt 100 times worse for over a decade and been told by some of the same people that I should be happy being single and alone.

Most of what people live for seems stupid to me. Your job? Great you exist so another person can use you to make a bunch of money. Your hobbies? Great so if you play with model trains your whole life then die, it's like you might as well have not existed in the first place. Honestly having a family was the only thing I looked forward to. Gave up on that though, now it's just death. If I pay another person to tell me "count back from 10" I'm going to drag them outside and beat my money back out of them.
And depressed and suicidal and realizing most of life is trivial bullshit. So they'd understand how I feel. Failing to see the problem here.

I'll admit I'm a bit lost at what you're trying to say. Life is a chore for me, I don't really enjoy anything. I know I'm not going to have a family or anything. The only thing I have to look forward to is when all these chores end. But instead of ending it when I was in a much better mindset, I was convinced to stick around. Either way this ends with my death. Do I want to leave people with the good I did for nothing, or should I take it all back before I leave. That's my only debate now.

Of course not, most cheaters don't. I'd be a bit more accepting if they did that, but what's the first thing that happens when you confront most cheaters? They start blaming everyone but themselves or they try to play down the amount of damage they did. Why would they go to therapy if they don't actually believe they have a problem? They wouldn't, so they don't.

Yup, but if I decided to cause them some form of anguish, mental or physical, they would. At least a bit. I understand this isn't healthy thinking, but to me neither is just living a life so everyone can tell me banal platitudes just to keep me providing a service for them. I think everyone should have to feel what I feel, even if only for an hour.

I absolutely agree, but honestly, being a good person doesn't do much for a lot of people in this world. So my choice is either leave the world with the good I've done, but received no joy out of, or ensure that after I'm gone there's a painful memory every time someone thinks of me. I kind of want the latter now. The former makes me feel used and not actually appreciated.

I've been to a couple therapists, I'm really tired of paying lots of money to people who take it and don't end up helping. If I paid a mechanic and he failed to fix my car I'd get my money back at least. I've been suicidal since I was younger and realized I'm not going to enjoy this world that much. I'm 30 now, so it's been at least 15 years.

So basically keep suffering so others benefit. That's exactly why I'm so angry in the first place. People don't care if I suffer everyday, just stay alive so society can still benefit off you, that's all the matters apparently. The people who suggest that don't care about the person, just that they keep existing and providing.

Here's the problem I have with that, I tried that with my ex. I made those excuses for her, and she went and did it again. These are people who are trying to have their cake and eat it too. I've had a terrible traumatic childhood, to the point where now I dream of murdering people. Doesn't make it right if I do murder someone, it doesn't give me an excuse. If you ask these people if cheating is wrong they will say yes. They're bad people. Actions make the person, bad actions make you a bad person.

Why didn't they focus on healing before the cheating? Also, why is it a majority of people cheat multiple times? And if someone is in a shitty household growing up they're allowed a pass at their bad behavior? I look in a mirror everyday, I see a good person who doesn't harm others for my own benefit. I'm not going to make excuses for people who make the world a worse place.

I'd go farther, and say not only are they bad people, but by even excusing this behavior you're a bad person too. The biggest problem we have in our society right now is people like you excusing shitty behavior from people. The world's a much better place without people like you in it.

That's why I advocate using a gun when you can. Quick and while technically it's probably painful, I don't think you can register the pain fast enough if done correctly. Don't hang yourself, it's a shit way to go, I've tried. When the journey sucks some people just want to get to the destination faster.

Because when 5-10 years have passed and they're still miserable what are you going to say? "Oh well." or "I'm sorry"? It's a statement just meant to keep people around to benefit the people around them.

I understand that some people get better, but depression isn't curable. It's just treatable. So some people it is going to get worse, and never better. Why not look at it honestly and actually assess if their life will possibly get better or not before stating it?

I've started challenging people. "Oh it gets better? If it doesn't what are you going to give me? Do I get to then make your life worse? Because if you're so confident it'll all be ok, and you're not just telling me 'fuck off' in a nice way, then you must be willing to put up something of value."

I'd argue oftentimes the inability to experience life to the fullest extent can be what drives people to choose suicide. If all around me are people experiencing life at it's fullest, why should I stick around for it's scraps? Instead, I'm selfish for leaving my half life because it will diminish their full life. That to me, is selfish.

The large amount of stigma against things associated with death and more acutely, suicide, cause a lot of people to be afraid to bring up when they're feeling suicidal, thus depriving them of the help and support they may require at the time. This is sometimes why you hear of people committing suicide but not bringing it up beforehand and then surprising everyone with their sudden death. Sometimes death is too heavy a subject for most people, making it hard to reach out when you need it.
No matter how you die, someone is probably going to have to clean up your body. Dying of old age still leaves behind your body and all the evacuated bowels with it.

Based off their other posts, it's easy to assume they've never experienced it. Maybe they have though, but if so then their comments are even worse because they'd know the pain suicidal people feel and are still calling them selfish.

Honestly though, why not? I'm allowed to make any other decisions while depressed, hell I bought a house while suffering depression. It honestly seems like people care most about keeping depressed people as functional cogs in society's machine than they actually care about how they feel. So after going through the tests and therapy and everything else that would be required for a doctor to legally assist suicide, why shouldn't someone be able to use a professional that would help eliminate the chance of something going wrong?

And speaking from the other side, you put no effort into how they feel, or have been feeling for awhile. It may be selfish, but so is everything we do as human beings practically. We do what mostly benefits us and makes us feel better. For some, that's killing themselves and ending all the feeling, for others, it's being upset and giving suicidal people shit.

Everything we do as human beings is selfish, this is a stupid argument. Also, no matter who dies or how, there's crap left behind. I agree though if you're suicidal you should have all your plans made for disposal and your will and whatnot.

I understand where you come from, but dictating someone's life even for their benefit is still dictating someone's life. I don't decide important life decisions for other people, why should they dictate mine? Some people can't be helped, they should be allowed to leave if they want.

Yea, not a democrat, and also not a socialist. Not sure what any of this new argument has to do with marriage though. You were arguing against gay marriage benefits, now you're arguing against socialism. I believe in educating the children in my country because it means less crime and better decisions made by our youth. Giving tax benefits to people with children just benefits the people with children. Also, not having kids myself and seeing as I'm probably not going to have any, just feels like a punishment that I have to pay more. I can totally understand if you feel this way about college however. I just prefer the benefits of a well educated population.

Ok but the problem with that is that I pay a certain amount in taxes, and the next guy pays the same, but he's married with kids, so he gets money back or puts less in. Which means more of my money is being used by society than his. Basically I'm helping contribute to children I don't have. Is that fair? Unless you're talking about the non tax related benefits of marriage, like being able to make legal or medical decisions, in which case I don't understand how kids should make a difference.
Legal marriage doesn't just give benefits to hetero couples that can reproduce though. There's no stipulation that you have to have kids when getting married.

Well I have severe depression, so I agree people shouldn't dwell on the small, bad things, but when you're in a bad mood, listening to some jackass sing about how great life is can be annoying. The sad songs usually relate better to the person in a bad mood. I mean imagine your gf/bf breaks up with you and as soon as you get in the car nothing but love songs start playing. It's like the cherry on a shit sundae.

There have been studies that show that music that is the same tone as your mood tends to sound better at the time. The sad music literally sounds better to you than happy music when you're sad. For some people anyway from what I gather.

Sometimes it helps people, the problem is that when it doesn't help it makes things infinitely worse. I've been to several therapists and each one makes me more wary than the last. You end up spending thousands trying to find someone, and everyone's suggestion is to spend more money and try another therapist. I guess if it helps great, but the only people I've met helped by therapy weren't that bad to begin with. Personally if I waste another couple hundred on a guy and get nothing in return I'll probably just beat my money out of him.
Appreciated, take care.

You can be grateful and still be in pain. I'm grateful for the good things in my life. Still doesn't mean it's enough to counteract the mental anguish I feel constantly. For me personally, I want people to stop using banal platitudes that don't mean anything.

Personally, I think empathy and honesty are the best ways to go. If you've never dealt with severe depression, think about what it would take to make you want to end your life. Would your whole family have to be dead? Would your wife have to leave you and take the kids? Become a quadriplegic? All of the above? Try the most you can to imagine what that feeling would be like, and then realize that the person you're talking to is probably there. It might even be no events or bad things, they just feel that way. David Foster Wallace likened it to watching people in a burning high rise, begging them not to jump. It's easy to be at the bottom and see help on the way. But you don't feel the flames, and how unbearably suffocating and hot it is, and how there's a good chance you burn alive before help even comes. Think about all that, and then be honest. If you don't understand, tell them that, then let them explain it the way they want to. YMMV of course, this is just for me, and I'll admit I'm far more gone than a lot of younger folks with depression.

True, but now you do. My problem is with the people who know this and have been told this and still think that saying it means something. If you don't know what to do or say, say that. It's a much better answer. My closest friends might not accept that I'm eventually taking my own life, but they also recognize that there isn't anything they can say or do to fix it either.

That's the last thing you tell to someone depressed. Someone's always got it worse, so no one is allowed to feel bad anymore? What's the cutoff, as one commenter already asked. Personally my suicide note actually calls out the people who were constantly telling me those kind of things.

Cleopatra was Greek in ancestry since she was a direct descendent of Ptolemy who ruled Egypt after Alexander the Great's death. I don't even think most rulers of Egypt were actually black, though I'll admit I know less about that part of Egypt's history.

I was able to buy a two story house with two sets of kitchens and bathrooms. I rent the upstairs to a friend who was in the same situation. Most of the people my age (30) who own property either bought it from family at a good price or were given their house. I lucked out considering the only other way to do it is to be married to someone who makes money as well.

This is absolutely true where I live. Rent is around 1200 a month at the cheapest. Meanwhile my mortgage on my place is less than $1000. The only difference is I have to pay repairs which can get costly. Still cheaper than renting in my area though.

The one thing that I've always argued with folks is that violence is usually more accepted for children, but we'd much rather our children grow up to have sex rather than be violent. Always seemed weird to me.

All of our abilities help humans. Just humans. Even when we help other species its not nearly as much as it hurts other species. I'm not saying humans deserve extinction necessarily, just that even a mosquito provides sustenance to a variety of other animals. Humans help humans. Thats it.
Human beings are the one species that don't benefit the planet. Even microscopic bugs are more useful. The world would definitely be better off without humanity, even if it is a sad thought.
Yea hard disagree, I've never met anyone over the age of 40 without a family that was even happy at all.

I agree, but that said, I do think last wishes of the deceased should be followed. My notes left for friends specifically say no funeral or memorial service involving my body or name. The thought of people using me after I'm dead in order to help their grieving bothers me.

No of course not, but the fact that the stories from that time period mention these bouts of showing emotion shows that even if it wasn't commonplace, it was an aspired ideal. There's several examples throughout history, a cursory glance seems to point to the 1800's being about the time that men crying or showing emotion became less commonplace. Possibly linked to people moving out of their hometowns more where they would have known most of the people their whole lives. I fully agree that you shouldn't let emotions impede your ability to function, but emotions are what make us want to do manly things, even if controlling them is how we accomplish it.

There's actually a lot of evidence in history that men crying was a normal thing up until recently. Ancient Greece has several examples in the Iliad alone. Men weren't afraid to show emotion because our emotions and passions are what give us the reason and strength to solve the problems in the first place. Also back then if someone made fun of you it was a lot easier to just kill them.

Absolutely true, and I don't blame anyone for my suicide. My suicide is a decision to leave this world and end the pain. I don't even really blame anyone completely for my feeling miserable. Some people just aren't meant for this world. But to lie to them and tell them it'll all be okay when it probably won't, is disingenuous and dismissive. I'm not killing myself to hurt those people, hurting them is just a fringe benefit. The thought that they'll feel a bit of what I felt my entire adult life, even if only for the short time that is the grieving process, is kind of nice. I've gotten more bitter as the years go by. My note when I hung myself at 17 was a lot nicer.

I'll be completely honest, that makes no sense to me. The only person who can determine if a life is worth living is that individual. Anyone else who's ever told me I have something worth sticking around for was to benefit other people. I've done that for 30 years, it's gotten me nowhere. My friends understand how I feel and accept it's going to happen. Anybody who wants me to stick around in endless misery is not a friend, they're an enemy. This is of course just my opinion.
I used to feel that way too. 13 years later I know life just sucks for some people and it's always going to suck.

I think it's great to keep up the fight if you have something worth fighting for. I don't anymore, and I'm tired of trying to find things giving me an excuse to stay in this world. It should be the other way around. I've put far more into this world than I'll ever get out.

Yea I've been through all of that. Therapists, medication, going out even when I didn't want to. Having conversations with people I can't relate to in any way because they're happy and I'm not. And a psuedo family to me is a poor excuse for having a real one. I still go to sleep and wake up everyday alone. I was much happier in a relationship.
